issue.title: Normalize missing `index: 0` in `/v1/embeddings` responses from upstream (e.g. Google Gemini)
issue.body:
### Problem
Some upstream providers (such as Google Gemini's OpenAI compatibility endpoint `/v1beta/openai/embeddings`) omit `"index": 0` on the first element in `data` (likely due to protobuf/Go zero-value `omitempty` serialization):

```json
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    { "object": "embedding", "embedding": [...] },
    { "object": "embedding", "index": 1, "embedding": [...] }
  ]
}
```

### Impact
The official `openai-python` SDK parses the missing field as `index = None`.
Downstream libraries/clients that sort results by index (e.g. `sorted(res.data, key=lambda x: x.index)`) crash with:
`TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'int' and 'NoneType'`

### Suggestion
In `internal/gateway/embeddings.go`, when returning a 200 OK embeddings response:
If `data[i]` is missing `index` or is `null`, fill `item["index"] = i`.
Can be done with `map[string]json.RawMessage` so embedding float vectors don't need to be decoded/re-encoded.

Happy to open a PR if this fits Magpie's scope.

comments.body:
Fixed in my fork: [38e36a7d](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/38e36a7d), branch `fix/embedding-indices`.

Successful embedding replies now fill only absent or null `data[i].index` with the array position. The raw JSON values keep float precision, base64 vectors, unknown fields, explicit zero and out-of-order indices. Both `/v1/embeddings` and `/embeddings` share it. Rerank and other retrieval replies keep their existing behavior.

The HTTP-handler regression failed against the old code for both missing and null indices on both aliases. Fixed tests pass, including related embedding/retrieval/rerank/transcription cases with `-race -count=3`. Additional cases keep complete and malformed replies byte-for-byte when no index needs filling.

No live Google request or openai-python SDK runtime was exercised; this verifies the JSON contract through a local vendor fixture.

Combined validation: all four changes and the earlier fix batch are in [0644f6fc](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/0644f6fc3dfbceedd3780315e1c21e8d23ee9ddb), branch `fix/issue-batch-20261023-b`, merged with upstream main `7aad6a50`. At that exact commit, full `go test -tags nogui ./... -count=1 -timeout=45m`, native/Linux/Windows vet and native/Linux/Windows builds all passed with Go 1.26.8, a temporary HOME, pinned Go caches and umask 027. The host was Linux; Windows checks were cross-build/vet. Full-suite evidence applies to this combined commit, with individual focused evidence above.

Fixed: `serveRetrieval` (internal/gateway/embeddings.go) relayed the vendor's embedding reply verbatim, so a provider that serializes `index` with omitempty (e.g. Google Gemini's OpenAI-compat `/v1beta/openai/embeddings`) sent back `data[0]` without `index`, and clients that sort by index crashed (`int` vs `NoneType`).

Change: on a 200 reply to `/embeddings` (both URL aliases normalize to this path), missing or null `data[i].index` is filled with the item's position; explicit indices (including 0 and out-of-order like 7), float precision, base64 vectors, unknown fields and usage are kept as the vendor said them. Rerank and transcription replies pass through unchanged.

Tests: `TestEmbeddingsSupplyMissingIndices` (red on unmodified code: `indices were not filled`), `TestEmbeddingIndicesPreserveOtherAnswers` (rerank, complete answers, malformed replies byte-for-byte). `gofmt -l` clean, `go build ./...` ok, `go vet -tags nogui ./internal/gateway/` ok. The full package run shows 5 pre-existing failures unrelated to this change (TestClaudeClientCacheAbsentUnchanged, TestCodexFittedImagesPastTheBudget, TestMarshalRawIsEncodingJSON, FuzzMarshalRaw seed#7, TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback), which fail identically on a clean upstream/main.

Branch: `fix/3302-embedding-indices`, commit `02a461098b32babecff8eedf07c52dee1328c0b2`. Fork branch ready for review; not a claim on ownership.
